name: Treasure & Keeping
content:
TREASURE

In Renaissance, money and other valuable possessions are abstracted as units of TREASURE. Treasure is generally earned or found in the course of completing Quests. Treasure is used to purchase equipment (see the Equipment section), but it is also spent regularly to maintain a character's Keeping:

KEEPING

The general degree of comfort and quality of gear a character is able to maintain for themselves is abstracted as their KEEPING. There are five Keeping tiers (defined below), each with its own benefits, drawbacks and cost in units of Treasure.

Your character's initial Keeping is set as part of the character creation process (see Character Creation) and determines your character's initial store of Treasure. Subsequently, Keeping is individual to each character during the Intermezzo phase but is shared by the party during the Quest phase.

KEEPING DURING INTERMEZZO

To maintain a given Keeping during an Intermezzo, a character must expend that Keeping tier’s cost for each month of the Intermezzo. If an Intermezzo lasts less than a month, reduce the cost by 1.

KEEPING DURING A QUEST

At the beginning of each Quest, the party must choose a Keeping and pay for it up front, multiplying the cost of that Keeping by the number of party members. The cost can be split among the party however they choose, but they must collectively spend that many units of Treasure before beginning the Quest. The Keeping persists for the duration of the Quest.

If the party wants to raise its Keeping mid-Quest, they must be in a location where provisions and gear are available and must pay the difference in cost between their current and desired tier, again multiplied by the number of party members. If the party spends no Treasure at the outset of the Quest, the Quest's Keeping is Wretched.

For example, if a party of three characters wants to maintain a Keeping of Comfortable for a Quest, they would multiply that Keeping's cost (3 Treasure) by the number of party members (3), arriving at a total cost of 9 Treasure. Each party member could pay 3 Treasure, or one could pay 5 and the others could pay 2 each, etc. Regardless of who pays what, a total payment of 9 Treasure means that, for the duration of the Quest, the party's Keeping will be Comfortable. If, in the middle of the Quest, the party finds themselves flush with Treasure when they visit a town that has provisions available, they could opt to spend an additional 3 Treasure (1 per party member) to upgrade the Quest's keeping from Comfortable to Opulent for the remainder of the Quest.

GRATUITI

Each Keeping includes GRATUITI, items that can be acquired, repaired, replenished or replaced without spending additional Treasure while a character maintains that Keeping. This represents the small purchases and provisioning that are assumed to be part of the cost to maintain that Keeping.

If your Keeping changes, you cannot keep anything provided by your previous Keeping's Gratuiti; You only have access to what's included in your current Keeping's Gratuiti.

KEEPING AS NARRATIVE TOOL

In addition to the mechanical effects defined below for each tier, Keeping is intended to serve as a narrative tool helping to provide contour to a character's journey, experience and self-expression in the campaign world. Whenever you or the party set a new Keeping, describe it.

KEEPING TIERS

The five tiers of Keeping are:

WRETCHED

Cost: 0

You live in inhumane conditions, sheltering wherever you can and relying on the kindness of strangers for sustenance. You do not have the resources to properly maintain or secure your equipment.

When Wretched on a Quest, you cannot regain Hope by resting. When Wretched during an Intermezzo, you cannot clear Conditions.

At the end of each Quest or Intermezzo you spend Wretched, check a Condition, then roll Craft, ill-favored, difficulty 10. On a failure, an important piece of your equipment is broken, lost or stolen and you check an additional Condition. If you roll Morte 💀, half of your Treasure (rounded up) is also stolen and you check one additional Condition.

Gratuiti: Nothing.

MODEST

Cost: 1

You live in humble but clean conditions and are able to purchase just enough food and drink to keep you healthy, but not much else. You’re able to maintain your equipment with some effort.

At the end of each Quest or Intermezzo you spend Modest, roll Craft, difficulty 10. On a failure, an important piece of your equipment is broken, lost or stolen and you check a Condition. If you roll Morte 💀, half of your Treasure (rounded up) is also stolen and you check one additional Condition.

Gratuiti: Plain clothes, humble food and drink, one simple tool or piece of traveling gear.

COMFORTABLE

Cost: 2

You live in pleasant conditions and get plenty to eat and drink. You can afford some finer clothing and can maintain your equipment without effort.

When Comfortable on a Quest, on each short rest, if you are not Helpless, you recover Endurance equal to twice your BODY score.

At the end of each Quest or Intermezzo you spend Comfortable, clear one Condition.

Gratuiti: Quality clothing, food and drink. A supply of simple tools and traveling gear.

PROSPEROUS

Cost: 3

You live in elevated conditions and have access to the finer things.

When Prosperous on a Quest, on each short rest, if you are not Helpless, you recover Endurance equal to three times your BODY score.

At the end of each Quest or Intermezzo you spend Prosperous, clear two Conditions and roll Awareness, difficulty 10. On a failure, an important or expensive piece of your equipment is stolen and you check a Condition. If you roll Morte 💀, half of your Treasure (rounded up) is also stolen and you check one additional Condition.

Gratuiti: Fine clothing, well-seasoned food and refreshing drink. Quality tools and traveling gear. A mount, if you choose.

OPULENT

Cost: 4

You want for nothing. Your lifestyle is lavish and conspicuous.

When Opulent on a Quest, on each short rest, if you are not Helpless, you recover Endurance equal to four times your BODY score, and after a long rest, you may clear one additional Condition.

At the end of each Quest or Intermezzo you spend Opulent, clear two Conditions and roll Awareness, ill-favored, difficulty 10. On a failure, an important or expensive piece of your equipment is stolen and you check a Condition. If you roll Morte 💀, half of your Treasure (rounded up) is also stolen and you check one additional Condition.

Gratuiti: The finest clothing, food and drink that can be procured - some from distant lands. An abundance of excellent tools and traveling gear. A mount and/or valet (noncombatant), if you choose.

EQUIPMENT & KEEPING

The concept of Keeping is also extended to equipment. Each equipment item has a designated Keeping, which defines its purchase cost and represents its general quality of construction. Additionally, equipment can be of six additional tiers - Uncommon, Rare, Very Rare, Exceptional, Wondrous, Singular - which cannot be set as a character or Quest's Keeping. See the Equipment section.
